title: Chilean great Alexis Sánchez signs with CF Montréal, continues career in MLS: Sources
content:
CF Montréal has signed Chilean forward Alexis Sánchez, sources briefed on the situation tell The Athletic.

Sánchez will be a designated player for Montréal. Chilean outlet El Deportivo LT first reported the player was signing with the Canadian club.

CF Montréal put up a teaser video for a new No. 10 signing on Monday evening, in which managing director Luca Saputo says “he wants Alexis, No. 10” on the jersey.

Sánchez, 37, has had a stellar career featuring stops at Barcelona, Arsenal, Manchester United, Inter Milan and many more. He spent last season with Sevilla in La Liga, with four goals and two assists in 28 appearances (1,308 minutes).

The forward is Chile’s all-time leading scorer (51 goals) and also holds the national record for appearances (168 caps).

Sánchez won league titles for Barcelona (2013), Inter Milan (2021, 2024) and Colo Colo (2006 Clausura, 2007 Apertura), where he began his career. He led Chile to two Copa America titles at the expense of Lionel Messi’s Argentina in the 2015 and 2016 finals. He also won two FA Cups with Arsenal (2015, 2017).

Montréal could use a boost of any kind. The club sits 14th in the Eastern Conference with 16 points after 18 matches but is seven points off the playoff line, albeit with plenty of games left in the regular season. Montréal’s 24 goals are tied for second-fewest in the conference.

Sánchez becomes the latest big-name player to feature for Montréal in MLS, joining the likes of Didier Drogba, Alessandro Nesta, Victor Wanyama, Ignacio Piatti and Marco Di Vaio, among others.
